Passage:
The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies. Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officers. The system has worked so well that it has been adopted in other countries too.
斯堪的纳维亚各国实行的开明的社会政策，受到全世界的推崇。在瑞典，已逐渐形成了一种完善的制度以保护每个公民不受专横的和不称职的政府官员的欺压。由于这种制度行之有效，已被其他国家采纳。
Public officials can make mistakes or act over-zealously even when they believe they are serving the public. Sweden established its parliamentary ombudsman institution in 1809. Today the Riksdag, or parliament, directly appoints four Parliamentary Ombudsmen, known collectively as JO. They make their decisions independently and supervise whether public authorities comply with the law. Legal advisers assess complaints, but not every complaint receives a full investigation. Complaint documents are generally open to public inspection, subject to rules protecting confidential information. The Ombudsmen can criticize improper official conduct and recommend legislative changes, but they cannot overturn court judgments or administrative decisions. The following teaching anecdote illustrates why checking the facts can matter more than simply accepting an official record.

2 in the belief that…，自以为……。
3 be qualified to do sth.，胜任做某事。

A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman complaining that he had been ill-treated by the police, simply because he was a foreigner. The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the Chief of Police in the district asking him to send a record of the case. There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner's complaint was justified and the Chief of Police strongly denied the accusation. The record did not provide enough evidence to substantiate the allegation, but when the Ombudsman received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village, he immediately sent one of his lawyers to investigate the matter. The lawyer ascertained that a policeman had indeed dealt roughly with foreigners on several occasions. The policeman’s prejudice against foreigners had not been apparent from the official record. It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts. The policeman in question was severely reprimanded and was informed that further proven misconduct could lead to prosecution. The Ombudsman's prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.

Step 3: Composition
Write a composition in about 300 words on the following topic:
• Describe the work of any one of the following: a policeman, a civil servant, a health officer, a social worker.
Key to composition
Plan and ideas for composition
Title: The work of a police officer
Introduction: Different attitudes to the police — appreciation and scrutiny can coexist.
What do police do?
Development: Number of jobs in one:
Traffic；keeping the peace; solving crime; helping to keep order in emergencies —air crashes, fires, road accidents, etc.
Conclusion: Respect demanding work while expecting accountability.
Composition
In Britain, people have different attitudes to the police. Some value the help they have received; others question particular actions or powers. Criticism does not in itself make someone a criminal. I think it is possible to appreciate the work of police officers while also expecting them to be accountable.
What does a policeman actually do? It is not an easy job to describe. After all, a policeman has a number of jobs in one. A policeman often has to control traffic, either on foot in the centre of a town, or in a police car on the roads. Indeed, in Britain, he might be in the Traffic Police and spend all, or a lot of, his time driving up and down main roads and motorways. A traffic policeman has to help keep the traffic moving, stop speeding motorists and help when there is an accident.
A policeman has to help keep the peace, too. If there is a fight or some other disturbance, we expect the police to come and assess the situation and restore order. And they often have to deal with situations at great risk to themselves and their own safety.
We expect the police to solve crimes, of course, so an ordinary policeman, even if he is not a detective, will often have to help identify and arrest suspects where there are legal grounds.
Police officers also work alongside other emergency services. At a road accident or a major incident, they may help secure the area and maintain order while firefighters or ambulance crews carry out their own duties. The appropriate service depends on the emergency; a fire is not simply a matter for the police.
Police work can be difficult and dangerous. I respect the effort involved, but that does not mean every action is beyond criticism. Protecting the public and being accountable to it should go together. I do not envy anyone who has to make difficult decisions under pressure in this job.

(b) They must investigate every complaint in full.
(c) They may overturn any court judgment.
(d) They make supervisory decisions independently.

(b) He was prosecuted.
(c) He was officially rebuked.

(c) Exactly two complaints are legally required before any investigation.
(d) All Swedish police officers are prejudiced against foreigners.

(a) Sweden
(b) In Sweden
(c) By Sweden
(d) To Sweden
6. Choose the indefinite noun phrase: If a citizen has ________, further investigation may follow.
(a) the complaint justifiably
(b) the justified complaint
(c) a justified complaint
(d) justified his complaint

(a) if
(b) although
(c) despite
(d) furthermore
8 If the Ombudsman hadn't acted promptly, this unpleasant practice ________.
(a) might have continued
(b) might continue
(c) will continue
(d) would continue
9. Choose the word closest to high-handed: The system protects individuals from ________ officials.
(a) efficient
(b) considerate
(c) overbearing
(d) handy
10 The action he takes ________ the nature of the complaint.
(a) depends on
(b) alternates with
(c) differs from
(d) agrees with
11. Choose the word closest to strongly in this context: The Chief of Police ________ denied the accusation.
(a) accidentally
(b) firmly
(c) mildly
(d) roughly
12. Choose the word meaning in question: The policeman ________ was severely reprimanded.
(a) questioned
(b) concerned
(c) absent
(d) interrogated

Step 3: Composition
Write a composition in about 300 words on the following topic:
• Describe the work of any one of the following: a policeman, a civil servant, a health officer, a social worker.
Key to composition
Plan and ideas for composition
Title: The work of a police officer
Introduction: Different attitudes to the police — appreciation and scrutiny can coexist.
What do police do?
Development: Number of jobs in one:
Traffic；keeping the peace; solving crime; helping to keep order in emergencies —air crashes, fires, road accidents, etc.
Conclusion: Respect demanding work while expecting accountability.
Composition
In Britain, people have different attitudes to the police. Some value the help they have received; others question particular actions or powers. Criticism does not in itself make someone a criminal. I think it is possible to appreciate the work of police officers while also expecting them to be accountable.
What does a policeman actually do? It is not an easy job to describe. After all, a policeman has a number of jobs in one. A policeman often has to control traffic, either on foot in the centre of a town, or in a police car on the roads. Indeed, in Britain, he might be in the Traffic Police and spend all, or a lot of, his time driving up and down main roads and motorways. A traffic policeman has to help keep the traffic moving, stop speeding motorists and help when there is an accident.
A policeman has to help keep the peace, too. If there is a fight or some other disturbance, we expect the police to come and assess the situation and restore order. And they often have to deal with situations at great risk to themselves and their own safety.
We expect the police to solve crimes, of course, so an ordinary policeman, even if he is not a detective, will often have to help identify and arrest suspects where there are legal grounds.
Police officers also work alongside other emergency services. At a road accident or a major incident, they may help secure the area and maintain order while firefighters or ambulance crews carry out their own duties. The appropriate service depends on the emergency; a fire is not simply a matter for the police.
Police work can be difficult and dangerous. I respect the effort involved, but that does not mean every action is beyond criticism. Protecting the public and being accountable to it should go together. I do not envy anyone who has to make difficult decisions under pressure in this job.
